findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on any I/O error, missing file, or permission denied
findings.failure_mode: untrusted filesystem input aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed error the caller can handle
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> and use map_err(|e| LoadError::Io(e))

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric input and on values exceeding u16::MAX
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV row or value > 65535 causes a hard panic in production
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError>, use parts.get(1).ok_or(ParseError::MissingField) and parse::<u16>().map_err(|_| ParseError::InvalidValue)

findings.problem: parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 is a lossy cast that silently truncates values > 65535
findings.failure_mode: a value like 70000 parses to u32 successfully, truncates to u16 as 4448, corrupting data without any error
findings.fix: parse directly as u16 with parse::<u16>().map_err(|_| ParseError::ValueOutOfRange) instead of parsing u32 then casting

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] use direct index access on an unbounded Vec with no bounds check
findings.failure_mode: empty or short CSV lines (missing columns, trailing newline) panic via index out of bounds
findings.fix: use parts.get(0) and parts.get(1) with ok_or(ParseError::MissingField), or replace split('').collect() with line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::Invalid)

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(...).collect() into parts Vec with parts[0]/parts[1] indexing instead of split_once
findings.failure_mode: allocates an intermediate Vec of all fields, then uses unchecked index access; split('').collect() pattern is forbidden for two-field records
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::Invalid)? to get name and value_str directly, avoiding intermediate allocation and indexing

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) performs console I/O inside a data-parsing function
findings.failure_mode: I/O is hidden inside what should be pure data processing, breaking Data/Calculations/Actions separation and making the function side-effectful and untestable
findings.fix: remove println! entirely; if logging is needed, return a separate log/result tuple from the shell layer, not from the parsing function

findings.problem: load_frames fuses file I/O (fs::read_to_string), console I/O (println), parsing, and domain construction into a single function
findings.failure_mode: violates Functional Core / Imperative Shell: the shell does file reads and logging while also doing parsing and domain construction; no separation between Actions, Calculations, and Data
findings.fix: split into: (1) shell layer that reads files and handles I/O errors, (2) pure parse function that takes a str and returns Result<Record, ParseError>, (3) domain types that are valid by construction

findings.problem: load_frames returns Vec<Record> with no error type; all failures must panic
findings.failure_mode: missing file, parse errors, and I/O errors all reach unwrap() panics with no typed error taxonomy for callers
findings.fix: define an enum LoadError { Io(std::io::Error), Parse(ParseError) } and return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>

findings.problem: Record{name: String, value: u16} stores raw primitives; name is an unchecked String and value is parsed from a raw string with lossy cast
findings.failure_mode: raw primitives cross the parse boundary without fallible smart constructors, so callers can construct invalid domain states directly; any String value and any truncated u16 is accepted
findings.fix: use a Name newtype with a smart constructor, define ParseError enum with Invalid/MissingField/ValueOutOfRange/Allocation variants, and validate inputs at the parse boundary before creating domain types

findings.problem: no domain cap validation, no try_reserve, no bounded allocation; intermediate Vec<String> allocated per line with no cap
findings.failure_mode: unbounded input can cause arbitrary heap allocation; allocation failures produce panics instead of typed Allocation errors
findings.fix: validate a trusted max_lines cap first, use Vec::new() then out.try_reserve(capacity).map_err(|_| ParseError::Allocation)?, and prefer split_once over intermediate Vec<String>

findings.problem: no benchmark, profiler, or allocation evidence exists for load_frames; file I/O and per-line Vec allocations are unmeasured
findings.failure_mode: performance characteristics are unknown; the per-line collect() into Vec<String> may dominate runtime for large inputs
findings.fix: add a criterion or custom benchmark measuring throughput (lines/sec) and allocation count, with a profiler to confirm hot path

findings.problem: no cargo fmt, cargo clippy, cargo test, or cargo check evidence exists for this crate
findings.failure_mode: formatting drift, lint violations, and compilation issues are undetected; strict source gate cannot be verified
findings.fix: run cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy -- -D warnings, and cargo test to establish a clean baseline

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_frames throughput or allocation characteristics
no profiler data (criterion, flamegraph, perf) for hot path analysis
no allocation tracking evidence (no try_reserve, no allocation budget)
no command-truth evidence: cargo fmt, cargo clippy, cargo test were not run
no second-ring evidence tying performance or safety claims to actual symbols/artifacts
residual_risk: The crate has 12 findings including 10 blockers: no error handling (all failures panic via unwrap), unchecked indexing on unbounded split results, a lossy u32-to-u16 cast that silently truncates, hidden console I/O in a data function, fused I/O/parsing/domain-construction violating Data/Actions separation, raw String domain field with no parse boundary, and no bounded allocation. Without all repairs, delivery is blocked.
